issues.legal_issue: A sale agreement signed only by the vendor may be a valid and enforceable contract when the vendor’s signature is genuine and the purchaser accepts the agreement.
material_facts: The vendor’s signature on the written agreement was found genuine on the basis of expert and witness evidence, and the reviewing court found no reason to disturb that factual finding.
The vendor signed and delivered the agreement to the purchaser, and four witnesses witnessed it.
The vendor acknowledged receipt of an initial payment on the agreement and later endorsed receipt of a further payment on it.
The purchaser accepted and acted on the agreement, and the evidence showed that the parties had concluded a contract.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was valid and enforceable even though only the vendor signed it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10 of the Contract Act, an agreement meeting the requirements for a contract is valid; the court found no applicable requirement that this sale agreement be written, signed by both parties, witnessed, or registered. A sale agreement is bilateral in its promises, but need not be signed by both parties: it may be oral, made through communications, or evidenced by a vendor-signed document delivered to and accepted by the purchaser. The court rejected the contrary views in S. M. Gopal Chetty v. Raman, AIR 1998 Madras 169, and Md. Mohar Ali v. Md. Mamud Ali, AIR 1998 Gauhati 92; it also explained that the latter decision incorrectly described a sale agreement as unilateral, referring to Calamari and Perillo, The Law of Contracts, 4th ed., paragraph 2-10(a).

rule.if: purchaser_specific_performance_claim and vendor_signed_agreement and vendor_delivered_agreement and purchaser_accepted_agreement

predicates.purchaser_specific_performance_claim: A purchaser sought to enforce a sale agreement through a claim for specific performance.
predicates.vendor_signed_agreement: The vendor signed the sale agreement, and the signature was established as genuine.
predicates.vendor_delivered_agreement: The vendor delivered the signed agreement to the purchaser.
predicates.purchaser_accepted_agreement: The purchaser accepted and acted on the delivered agreement.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeks specific performance and the vendor signed and delivered the agreement that the purchaser accepted, the agreement is enforceable even without the purchaser’s signature.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who has performed the purchaser’s obligations and established readiness and willingness to pay the balance is entitled to specific performance under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
material_facts: The purchaser paid the earnest money and part of the purchase price.
The purchaser sent a notice expressing readiness and willingness to pay the balance of the consideration, and the vendor acknowledged the notice.
The trial court and the appellate court found that the purchaser had performed her part and fulfilled the requirements of Section 16(c).
issues.conclusion: The purchaser satisfied Section 16(c) and was entitled to the decree for specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires the claimant to establish performance, or continuous readiness and willingness to perform, the essential contractual obligations required of that claimant. The court upheld the findings that the purchaser had performed her part and had conveyed readiness and willingness to pay the balance.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_paid_earnest_money and purchaser_notified_readiness_to_pay_balance and seller_acknowledged_readiness_notice

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit seeking specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_paid_earnest_money: The purchaser paid the earnest money and part of the purchase price.
predicates.purchaser_notified_readiness_to_pay_bala: The purchaser sent a notice conveying readiness and willingness to pay the remaining consideration.
predicates.seller_acknowledged_readiness_notice: The vendor acknowledged the purchaser’s notice of readiness and willingness.

issues.definition: In a specific performance suit, a purchaser who paid the earnest money, notified the vendor of readiness to pay the balance, and had that notice acknowledged is entitled to specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to establish that the purchaser was put in possession of part of the property does not defeat specific performance when the agreement is enforceable and the purchaser has satisfied the other requirements for relief.
material_facts: The purchaser claimed to have been put in possession of part of the property, but that claim was not accepted by the trial court.
The court upheld the finding that the agreement was valid and enforceable and that the purchaser had satisfied the other requirements for specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The failure to establish part performance by delivery of possession did not prevent the decree for specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 and held that, where the agreement is enforceable and the purchaser has satisfactorily established the other requirements for specific performance, failure to prove delivery of possession does not defeat the claim. The court cited no earlier case for this point.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_possession_not_established and enforceable_sale_agreement and purchaser_satisfied_other_specific_performance_requirements

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit seeking specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_possession_not_established: The purchaser’s claim to have been put in possession of part of the property was not established.
predicates.enforceable_sale_agreement: The evidence established an enforceable sale agreement between the vendor and purchaser.
predicates.purchaser_satisfied_other_specific_perfo: The purchaser established the other requirements for obtaining specific performance, including performance and readiness and willingness to perform the purchaser’s obligations.

issues.definition: In a specific performance suit, the lack of proof that the purchaser was put in possession does not bar relief when the agreement is enforceable and the purchaser has satisfied the other requirements for specific performance.
